minutes.headline: Planning Board put off the solar bylaw to fall for more public input and named Paula Bertram to MRPC.
minutes.summary: The board reviewed the 33-response solar survey and leaned toward taking more time with listening sessions rather than rushing a spring bylaw. It approved two sets of minutes and voted a regional planning representative. It also discussed the earth removal bylaw, stormwater bylaw updates and a rewrite of the subdivision rules, and set aside the tree-clearing bylaw.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted to nominate Paula Bertram as its representative to MRPC, and the motion passed.
The board leaned toward more public input on the solar bylaw: a listening session in March or early April, and a fall town meeting as the target.
The board set the tree-clearing bylaw aside to focus on the master plan, and asked the planner to bring the earth removal bylaw back for the next or first February meeting.
The board heard that its master plan grant application was not funded; funds from last year's capital request remain.
The planner was asked to start drafting the master plan RFP for the non-population components.

why_it_matters: A solar bylaw is now unlikely to reach voters before a fall town meeting, so residents have until the listening session to shape it.
The earth removal bylaw is aimed at annual town meeting, and a member raised that engineering costs for permits could fall on homeowners doing small removals.
The master plan will rely on money already appropriated, since the grant was not awarded, and the board wanted deliverables before asking for more.
